snip.t: This elevated pressure is due to a combination of increased pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), increased pulmonary blood flow, and/or increased left atrial pressure.
Because pulmonary vascular resistance is high, most of this blood passes through the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta rather than flowing through the lungs.

snip.t: Pulmonary vasculature (arterioles & veins) – thin‑walled muscular vessels: Fibrotic distortion narrows vessels, raising pulmonary vascular resistance → secondary pulmonary hypertension and right‑heart strain (cor pulmonale).
It often appears after a few days, once the pulmonary vascular resistance falls.
Chronic increases in pulmonary vascular resistance lead to RV hypertrophy and eventual dilatation and failure.
Mechanism: pulmonary vascular resistance fails to fall after birth; right-to-left shunting through fetal channels bypasses the lungs and causes hypoxaemia.

Must know: RDS = surfactant deficiency; TTN = retained fetal lung fluid; MAS = airway obstruction plus chemical pneumonitis; caffeine treats apnoea of prematurity; PPHN = failure of the normal postnatal fall in pulmonary vascular resistance.

qs.q: Why do the fetal lungs have high pulmonary vascular resistance prior to birth?
o: The ductus venosus shunts all blood from the heart
The fetal lungs are filled with fluid and not exchanging
The placenta actively secretes vasoconstrictive agents
The left ventricle generates higher systemic pressures
qs.e: Because the fetal lungs are filled with fluid and not performing gas exchange, they maintain high pulmonary vascular resistance. Most blood bypasses the lungs via the fetal shunts rather than due to placental prostaglandins.
qs.s: Neonatology 1: Newborn Assessment and Essential Newborn Care: MCQs

qs.q: Immediately following birth, a newborn takes its first breath, causing pulmonary vascular resistance to drop and left atrial pressure to exceed right atrial pressure. What is the direct mechanical consequence?
o: Septum primum retracts into superior vena cava
Muscular walls of septum secundum undergo fusion
Fibrotic tissue completely obliterates ostium primum
Flap valve of foramen ovale is pressed shut
Endocardial cushions swell to seal the left canal
qs.e: Increased left atrial pressure pushes the septum primum against the septum secundum, functionally closing the foramen ovale.

qs.q: Which maneuver is used to reduce pulmonary vascular resistance during a tet spell?
qs.e: Knee‑to‑chest increases SVR and reduces PVR during a tet spell. Phenylephrine is not the first line.
